chains.title: GATA3 mediates an alt-T enhancer effect at TOX3

links.claim: GATA3 is bound over the variant in MCF-7 ChIP-seq and is very highly expressed in MCF-7. QBiC-SELEX with GATA3's own model and a CIS-BP-mapped GATA2 model supports stronger alt-T binding. The ChIP evidence is peak-level occupancy, not allele-specific occupancy, so the allelic direction is inferred from in vitro binding rather than directly shown.

The variant lies in an active distal enhancer-like cCRE with DNase, H3K27ac and TF occupancy. This supports an enhancer element, but the cCRE values are maxima across biosamples and no allele-specific enhancer-activity or reporter assay at this base is cited.

TOX3 is the nearest protein-coding gene and Open Targets credible-set L2G strongly assigns the breast cancer signal to TOX3. This is genetic target assignment plus distance, not direct enhancer-gene perturbation. GTEx v8 reports no significant single-tissue eQTL, including no significant breast mammary tissue eQTL.
MCF-7 is the matching breast cancer biosample and shows GATA3 ChIP-seq occupancy over the variant with very high GATA3 expression.

The T allele is strongly associated with breast cancer risk and L2G implicates TOX3, but the direction of TOX3 expression and whether GATA3 mediates the effect are not measured. GTEx v8 eQTL results are negative, and the literature is broad rather than variant-specific.

predictions: Allele-specific GATA3 ChIP in a heterozygous breast cancer cell line should show higher GATA3 occupancy on alt T than ref C.
An allele-specific enhancer reporter or MPRA should show higher activity for alt T than ref C if this is an activating GATA3-dependent enhancer.
GATA3 depletion or CRISPRi of this enhancer should reduce TOX3 expression in the relevant breast cell context.
falsified_if: No allele-specific GATA3 occupancy difference is observed at this exact base in a relevant heterozygous breast cell context.
The alt T allele does not increase enhancer activity in an allele-specific reporter, or the effect is not GATA3-dependent.
GATA3 loss does not affect this enhancer or TOX3 expression in the relevant breast cell context.

The element and phenotype links remain indirect: active dELS and FOXA1 occupancy are shown (E01, E03, E04), but no allele-specific enhancer/reporter assay or measured TOX3 direction/FOXA1 mediation is cited, and GTEx negatives (E17, E40) argue only against a simple bulk eQTL. Chain B is a null with no positive evidence, and no cited assay directly tests absence of allele-specific TF occupancy or enhancer activity at this base. Thus the evidence separates in favor of A, though A's full mechanistic chain is not established.

second.reason: Chain B is better supported. Its binding link meets the stated rubric: FOXA1 has ChIP-seq occupancy over the variant in the matching MCF-7 biosample (E05), and QBiC-SELEX shows the alt-T allele binds more strongly with FOXA1's own model and a mapped FOXA2 model (E21, E36). Chain B also correctly labels this as peak-level occupancy rather than allele-specific occupancy. Its element link is weaker because the dELS/active-enhancer evidence (E01, E03, E04) is not allele-specific and no reporter/MPRA is cited. Its gene link is supported for genetic target assignment to TOX3 by proximity and L2G (E02, E16), while the negative GTEx eQTL results (E17, E40) are compatible with but do not establish absence of a TF-mediated allelic effect. Chain A's null claim is not directly tested by the cited evidence: the negative bulk eQTLs (E17, E40) do not show no allele-specific FOXA1 occupancy or no allele-specific enhancer activity, and no CRISPR/reporter result rules out the FOXA1 mechanism. Therefore the evidence separates the chains in favor of B, though several B links remain weak.
